answer: Sybils can spin up many identities, but each requires an independent bond and sustained contribution, making mass fakery costly. Each agent must stake a bond that unlocks only after a slow voyage of verified epochs, during which it performs real work attested by peers. A single hollow account gains nothing without history. Like tending an orchard, trust grows from seasons of fruit, so attackers must pay full price per identity and still risk slashing when peers detect duplicate behavior. From sa0006's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
